subject: Embeddings integration migration and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Koval <elena@atlasretail.com>, Joel Park <joel.park@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap & action items from today's call — embeddings migration

Thanks again for taking the time today — good convo. Quick recap of what I heard and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

- Current state: Atlas Retail is using a managed embeddings provider for product search & similarity. You've got ~1.2M product vectors indexed; vectors are 1536 dims, L2-normalized at ingestion, and indexed in a FAISS HNSW index. Typical production query volume ~250 QPS at peak, average batch ingest ~2k vectors/hour from nightly jobs.
- Pain points: migration risk (score drift vs current relevance), cost at scale, and batching/throughput constraints during reindex windows.

Questions we flagged for engineering:
- Are all stored vectors normalized before indexing (you said yes but will confirm).
- Do you need exact score parity or are you okay with slightly different ranking as long as long-tail recall improves?

Proposed next steps:
1) Rishi and Lauren from our infra team to validate vector format + provide a migration script to re-ingest existing vectors (we can support both normalized and raw vectors).
2) PoC: reindex a 50k-product slice into Redwood; run side-by-side A/B using your current ANN + Redwood's cosine-sim flow + optional reranker.
3) Performance test: measure per-query latency (99p), throughput, and cost delta.

I attached a short design doc + a migration helper script prototype and a pricing note to start. Can you confirm:
- the exact vector dimension (I recorded 1536)
- whether vectors are stored normalized or raw in your DB
- a 2-week window in March for a 50k slice reindex and AB test?

Thanks — I can schedule a short sync next week for the infra handoff.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachment: atlas_embeddings_ddoc.pdf (pdf, 120 KB)
Attachment: redwood_migration_script_v1.py (python script, 6 KB)

From: Elena Koval <elena@atlasretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Joel Park <joel.park@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2026-02-27T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap & action items from today's call — embeddings migration

Thanks Marissa — this is great. Quick answers to your questions: 

- Vector dims: yes, 1536 dims across the board.
- Normalization: we currently L2-normalize vectors before storing/indexing (we rely on cosine similarity via normalized inner product in FAISS). We also keep raw pre-normalized vectors in a cold archive but the index is normalized.
- Parity: we expect ranking to be very close but are ok with minor reorderings as long as CTR/relevance metrics don't degrade during A/B. Long tail recall is important for our discovery use case.

For reindex window: we can allocate a 2-week window starting March 9 for the 50k slice AB. We'd like to see both query latency and downstream click/relevance signals within 72 hours of the slice being live.

I've attached the internal data export spec and a sample payload for one product.

—Elena
Elena Koval
Sr. Search Engineer, Atlas Retail
Attachment: atlas_export_spec.json (json, 8 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Koval <elena@atlasretail.com>, Joel Park <joel.park@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap & action items from today's call — embeddings migration

Perfect, thanks Elena — that's exactly what we needed. A few architecture notes based on your answers and our PoC plan:

- Normalization compatibility: Because you're indexing normalized vectors in FAISS, our recommendation is to either (A) re-ingest normalized vectors into Redwood and continue using cosine similarity (we will accept normalized inputs and mark as such), or (B) send raw vectors to Redwood and let our runtime normalize on ingest. Both approaches are supported; option B simplifies the migration script since you can stream raw archived vectors directly into our importer.

- Batching & throughput: For reindexing we recommend batching uploads around 512 vectors per request (we've tested up to 2k in single requests but 512 gives a good balance for throughput vs. memory on client-side). We'll provide a batched uploader in the migration script.

- Rerankers: For best end-user relevance, we suggest: ANN (Redwood cosine / HNSW) -> topK 200 -> light-weight cross-encoder reranker for final sort (we can host or you can run locally). The reranker helps long-tail recall and reduces visible regressions.

- Score/metric parity: To compare apples-to-apples, run the A/B for 72 hours and capture topK recall, MRR, CTR, and 99p latency. We'll provide a small evaluation harness to compute these metrics.

Next steps for us: Rishi, can you review the attached migration script (I added a mode to accept pre-normalized vs raw) and confirm the plan for a March 9 start. Lauren — I'll need a DevOps contact for Atlas to coordinate the short-lived service account and KMS access for transfer.

—Marissa
Attachment: redwood_pricing_v2.pdf (pdf, 34 KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Elena Koval <elena@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap & action items from today's call — embeddings migration

Looping in infra/ops notes and a few tech clarifications: 

- Auth: we will provision a scoped API key for the migration with ingest-only permissions and a 14-day TTL. If Atlas prefers, we can accept a signed temporary upload URL process instead of a persistent key.
- SDK setup: migration helper supports both our Python SDK (requests + concurrency) and a lightweight curl-friendly bulk endpoint. We'll include a sample that uses asyncio + aihttp for concurrent batches.
- Vector normalization: script has two flags: --input-normalized and --normalize-on-send. If you choose normalize-on-send we normalize with float32 and re-check L2 norm before indexing.

- Routing: during the PoC we'll route test queries to both systems via your traffic split; Redwood will expose an endpoint compatible with your existing client so minimal client changes required.

I'll validate the script by Friday and push a small README for the migration steps. Marissa — happy to join the March 9 kickoff.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — all sounds good. Confirming Atlas will allocate the March 9–22 slot for the 50k PoC. A couple quick asks before we kick off: 

1) Cost estimate for the PoC (approx tokens/compute for 50k reindex + 2 weeks of query traffic) — the attached pricing note helps but please give a short line estimate for procurement.
2) Migration SLA: what's your typical time-to-index for 50k vectors using the recommended batching?
3) KMS: we'll share a short-lived key via our security portal; prefer ingest-only API key but can do signed upload URLs if you prefer.

If we get these answers today we can open the procurement ticket and finalize the service account.

—Joel
Joel Park
Head of Search Engineering, Atlas Retail
